αἰγιόχοιο: αἰγίοχος — aegis-bearing (of Zeus); epic gen. sg. -οιο (= Attic -ου); meaning disputed: usually ’holding the αἰγίς (goatskin shield)’, other derivations were proposed in antiquity
αἰπὺν: αἰπύς — steep, sheer; masc. acc. sg.
αἵ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. pl. (αἵ μοι ἕποντο ’which followed me’)
αὐτοί: αὐτός — self; intensive pron., masc. nom. pl.: ’themselves’
αὐτὴν: αὐτός — self; fem. acc. sg.: ’her’ · also intensive, accusative subject of an infinitive: ’she herself’ (αὐτὴν ποθέσαι ’that she herself miss [him]’)
αὐτῇ: αὐτός — self; intensive pron., fem. dat. sg.: ’for herself’ · also plain anaphoric pronoun referring to a thing, dat. sg. with ἐν: ’in it’ (ἐν αὐτῇ, of the ship)
αὐτῷ: αὐτός — self; masc. dat. sg.: ’himself’, reinforcing a personal pronoun (σοὶ δ’ αὐτῷ ’to you yourself’)
αὖ: αὖ — again, in turn, back; adv., shorter form of αὖτε
αὖθι: αὖθι — there, on the spot, right there; adv.
αὖτ: αὖτε (elided αὖτ’) — again, in turn, moreover; epic adv./conj.
αὖτε: αὖτε — again, in turn, on the other hand; adv.
βασίλεια: βασίλεια — queen, princess; fem. voc. sg., address to Penelope
βοὸς: βοῦς — ox, cow, heifer; gen. sg.
γ: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle (elided γ’)
γέροντα: γέρων — old man, elder; masc. acc. sg.
γε: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle
γενέσθαι: γίγνομαι — become, be born; aor. inf.: ’to have been born’
γλαυκῶπις: γλαυκῶπις — epithet of Athena: ’gleaming-eyed’ (or ’owl-eyed’; sense uncertain); fem. nom. sg.
γόοιο: γόος — wailing, lament; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
δέμας: δέμας — bodily form, frame; neut. acc. sg., accusative of respect: ’in body’
δήμῳ: δῆμος — district, land, people; dat. sg.
δαναοῖσιν: Δαναοί — the Danaans (a name for the Greeks); masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι(ν)
δεῦρ: δεῦρο — hither, here; adv., elided (δεῦρ’ = δεῦρο)
δόρπον: δόρπον — evening meal, supper; neut. acc. sg.
δώματ: δῶμα — house, home; neut. acc. pl., elided (δώματ’ = δώματα)
δώματα: δῶμα — house, dwelling; neut. acc. pl. (plural for a single dwelling): ’house, home’
δὴ: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
εἰ: εἰ — if; conditional conj. · also introducing an indirect question after a verb of asking or telling: ’whether’ (εἰ δή ’whether indeed’) · also in εἰ δ’ ἄγε, an interjectional idiom with the imperative: ’come now, well then’
εἰδὼς: οἶδα — know; perf. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’knowing’
εἰν: ἐν (epic εἰν before a vowel) — in, on; + dat.
εἰποῦσ: εἶπον — say, speak; aor. part. fem. nom. sg., elided (εἰποῦσ’ = εἰποῦσα)
εἰπὼν: εἶπον — say, speak; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.
εἰς: εἰς — into, to; prep. + acc. · also εἰμί ’be’: pres. 2 sg., epic (= Attic εἶ): ’you are’ (τίς … εἰς; ’who are you?’)
εἴ: εἰ — if; conditional conj. (accented εἴ before a following enclitic, περ among them) · also introducing an indirect question, ‘whether’ (τίς δ’ οἶδ’ εἴ κέ ... ‘who knows whether’)
εἴπεσκε: εἶπον (aor. of λέγω/φημί) — say, speak; iterative impf. 3 sg. with suffix -σκε, epic (= ἔλεγεν ἄν): ’would say, used to say’
εὐρύκλεια: Εὐρύκλεια — Eurycleia, Odysseus’s old nurse; nom. sg.
εὐρὺ: εὐρύς — wide, broad; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’widely’ · also attributive, agreeing with a neut. noun: ’wide’ (κλέος εὐρύ ’wide fame’)
εὔνησε: εὐνάω — lay to rest, put to bed (causative of εὕδω); aor. act. 3 sg.
ζώει: ζώω (Attic ζάω) — live, be alive; pres. 3 sg.
θ: τε (elided and aspirated θ’ before rough breathing, cf. ἔφαθ’) — and; connective particle
θάρσει: θαρσέω — be of good courage, take heart; pres. imper. 2 sg.
θανάτοιο: θάνατος — death; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
θείοιο: θεῖος — divine, godlike; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
θεράποντες: θεράπων — attendant, servant; masc. nom. pl.
θοὴν: θοός — swift, quick; fem. acc. sg.
θυμολέοντα: θυμολέων — lion-hearted; masc. acc. sg., compound epithet (θυμός + λέων)
θυμόν: θυμός — heart, spirit, soul; acc. sg.
θῖνα: θίς — shore, beach; fem. acc. sg.
κέλευθα: κέλευθος — path, way, course; neut. nom./acc. pl. κέλευθα, epic by-form beside fem. sg. κέλευθος
κέν: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν); accented before an enclitic
καθ: κατά (elided καθ’) — down, throughout; prep. + acc., aspirated before rough breathing
κακὸν: κακός — bad, evil; masc./neut. acc. sg.: ’by an evil (fate)’, inner acc. with μόρον · also neut. nom. sg., subject of an impersonal verb (τι … κακὸν … μελέτω ’let no evil thing be a care’) · also neut. acc. sg. as a plain substantive, direct object: ’harm, evil’ (κακὸν ἀλλοδαποῖσι φέροντες ’bringing harm to men of other lands’)
καλὸν: καλός — beautiful, fair, fine; masc. acc. sg. (agreeing with a noun) · also neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’beautifully’ (with an infinitive) · also neut. acc. sg. used as a noun, direct object: ’a fine one’ (μάλα καλὸν ἑλών) · also neut. acc. sg., attributive, agreeing with a stated neut. noun: ’fine’ (καλὸν δέπας ’the fine cup’)
κατάλεξον: καταλέγω — recount in full and in order (not yet ’choose’, as later); aor. imper. 2 sg.
κατὰ: κατά — down, throughout, in; prep. + acc.; also as preverb in tmesis (κατὰ … ἤσθιον = κατήσθιον ’devoured’) · also ’according to, in conformity with’ (κατὰ μοῖραν ’according to what is fitting’) · also + acc., ’in quest of, after’ (κατὰ ληίδα ’in quest of plunder’)
κεκασμένον: καίνυμαι — excel, surpass; perf. pass. part. masc. acc. sg., + dat.: ’distinguished (by)’
κεν: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + secondary indic. (κατέφθιτο), unreal past conditional: ’would have perished’ · also + aor. indic. of a future event pictured as already accomplished, an eventual near-certainty rather than a counterfactual: ἤ κεν ... κτεῖνεν ’or he may well have killed (him) already’
κεῖνον: κεῖνος — that, that one; demonstrative pron., epic (= Attic ἐκεῖνος); masc. acc. sg.
κεῖνόν: κεῖνος — that, that one; demonstrative pron., epic (= Attic ἐκεῖνος); masc. acc. sg. (accented on the ultima before the enclitic γ’)
κλέος: κλέος — fame, renown, report; neut. nom. sg. · also neut. acc. sg. (same form), direct object: μέγα κλέος ἤρατο ’won great fame’; κλέος φέρειν ’bring report’
κλαίειν: κλαίω — weep, mourn; pres. inf.: ’to weep’
κλαίουσα: κλαίω — weep, cry; pres. part. fem. nom. sg.: ’weeping’
κλῦθί: κλύω — hear, listen; aor. imper. 2 sg., + gen.: ’hear me!’
κούρη: κούρη — girl, daughter; fem. nom. sg.
κούρῃ: κούρη — girl, maiden, daughter (Attic κόρη); dat. sg.
λίην: λίαν — very much, exceedingly; adv., Ionic λίην (= Attic λίαν)
λευκὰ: λευκός — white, bright; neut. acc. pl.
μ: ἐγώ — I; encl. acc. sg., elided (μ’ = με): ’me’ · also = dat. μοι, elided before a vowel, with a dat. participle: ’to me’ (ἥ μ’ οἴῳ ἔρροντι συνήντετο, συναντάω + dat.)
μάλα: μάλα — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.
μέγαν: μέγας — great, big, tall; masc. acc. sg.
μέγαρα: μέγαρον — hall, great room; neut. acc. pl.
μέν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ (the acute μέν is kept before a following enclitic; elsewhere μὲν) · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’ (οὐ μέν ’not indeed’)
μένον: μένω — wait, wait for; impf. 3 pl., unaugmented
μέσον: μέσος — middle, mid-; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially with a place-name: ’mid-Argos’ · also as an ordinary attributive adjective agreeing with a neuter noun: ’the middle of the sail’ (μέσον ἱστίον)
μή: μή — not; negative particle (used with imperatives and subjunctives, unlike οὐ) · also introducing a negative purpose/fear clause with the optative in secondary sequence: μή ἑ λάθοι ’lest he should escape notice’
μακάρεσσι: μάκαρ — blessed, happy (epithet of the gods); masc./fem. dat. pl., epic -εσσι (= Attic -σι)
μεγάροισιν: μέγαρον — hall, great room, house; neut. dat. pl., epic -οισι(ν), plural for a single house
μεγάρῳ: μέγαρον — hall, great room; neut. dat. sg.
μεγαλήτορος: μεγαλήτωρ — great-hearted, great of spirit (μέγας + ἦτορ ’heart’); masc. gen. sg.
μελαίνῃ: μέλας — black; standing epithet of ships; fem. dat. sg. μέλαινα · also modifying a different noun, not a ship (μελαίνῃ φρικί ’with a dark ripple’, of the sea’s surface)
μερμήριξε: μερμηρίζω — ponder, devise, turn over in the mind; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἐμερμήριξε)
μετέειπε: μετεῖπον — speak among, address; aor. 3 sg., epic uncontracted, augment ἐ- kept (= Attic μετεῖπε)
μετὰ: μετά — among, with, after; prep. + dat./acc./gen. · with acc. also ’in quest of, in search of’ (μετὰ χαλκόν ’after bronze’)
μευ: ἐγώ — I; encl. gen. sg., epic μευ (= Attic μου): ’of me’, with κλύω ’hear me’
μηδέ: μηδέ — and not, nor, do not; neg. conj., used to forbid before an imperative
μηδὲ: μηδέ — and not, nor; negative conj., companion to μή
μηρί: μηρίον — thigh-piece, burned as an offering; neut. acc. pl., elided (μηρί’ = μηρία)
μηχανόωνται: μηχανάομαι — contrive, devise, scheme; pres. 3 pl., epic uncontracted -όωνται (= Attic -ῶνται): ’they contrive’
μιν: μιν — him, her, it; epic encl. acc. pron. (= Attic αὐτόν/αὐτήν/αὐτό)
μνῆσαι: μιμνήσκω — remind; mid. remember, be mindful; aor. imper. mid. 2 sg.: ’remember!’
μοι: ἐγώ — I; encl. dat. sg.: ’to me, for me’
μοῖραν: μοῖρα — due share, what is fitting, portion, fate; fem. acc. sg. (κατὰ μοῖραν ’according to what is fitting’)
μυθήσασθαι: μυθέομαι — speak, tell, declare; aor. inf. mid.
μὲν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ
μὴ: μή — not; negative particle in wishes, prohibitions, and purpose/fear clauses · also negating a conditional clause after εἰ: εἰ μὴ ’if not, unless’
μᾶλλον: μάλα — very, much; comparative adv. μᾶλλον: ’more, rather, the more’
μῦθον: μῦθος — word, speech, thing said; acc. sg.
νήπιος: νήπιος — infant, still a child, witless; masc. nom. sg.
ναίων: ναίω — dwell, inhabit; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’dwelling’
νῆα: ναῦς — ship; acc. sg., epic νῆα
οἰκία: οἰκίον — house, home (Homer only in neut. pl. οἰκία, collective, = Attic οἰκία fem. sg.); neut. acc. pl.
οἱ: οἱ — encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him’ (very common) · also ὁ, ἡ, τό ’he, she, it’, masc. nom. pl. ’they’ (e.g. οἱ μὲν … οἱ δέ ’some … others’)
οἴχεται: οἴχομαι — be gone, have departed; pres. with perf. sense, 3 sg.: ’is gone’
οἶδεν: οἶδα — know; perf. 3 sg. (with pres. sense): ’knows’
οὐδ: οὐδέ (elided οὐδ’) — and not, nor, not even
οὐδέ: οὐδέ — and not, nor, not even; neg. conj.
οὐδὲ: οὐδέ — and not, nor, not even; neg. conj. (grave, mid-clause form)
οὐκ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., form before a vowel with smooth breathing (οὐχ before a rough breathing)
οὐλοχύτας: οὐλοχύται — barley scattered on a sacrificial victim (οὐλαί + χέω ’pour’); fem. acc. pl.
οὔ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., in a question expecting the answer ’yes’ · also the plain negative adverb in a declarative statement, with no question implied: ’not’
οὔτ: οὔτε (elided οὔτ’) — nor, and not; correlative negative conj.
οὔτε: οὔτε — nor, and not; correlative negative conj.
πάμπρωτον: πάμπρωτος — first of all, very first; adj., neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’first of all’
πάντα: πᾶς — all, every; neut. nom./acc. pl.
πάντας: πᾶς — all, every; masc. acc. pl.
πάρος: πάρος — before, formerly; adv., with inf. like Attic πρίν · also a plain temporal adverb with a finite verb, not paired with an infinitive: ’formerly, in the past’ (αἳ πάρος ἦσαν ’who formerly were’)
πέμπε: πέμπω — send, send off; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented: ’was sending’
πίονα: πίων — fat, rich; neut. acc. pl., agreeing with νῶτα: ’fat’
πίονας: πίων — fat, rich; masc./fem. acc. pl. (fem. usually πίειρα)
παιπαλοέσσης: παιπαλόεις — rugged, craggy; fem. gen. sg. παιπαλοέσσης, agreeing with Χίοιο (the island-name Chios treated as feminine)
παλλὰς: Παλλάς — Pallas, title of Athena of unknown origin (perhaps πάλλω ’brandish’); nom. sg.
παντοίῃς: παντοῖος — of every kind, of all sorts; fem. dat. pl.
παρὰ: παρά — beside, along, from; prep. + dat./acc./gen. · also used as an adverb with no case expressed: ’beside, alongside’ (παρὰ … ἐτάνυσσε τράπεζαν ’drew a table up beside (them)’)
πατρίδα: πατρίς — native land, fatherland; fem. acc. sg. (φίλην ... πατρίδα γαῖαν ’his dear fatherland’)
παύσασθαι: παύω — stop, cease; aor. mid. inf., + gen.: ’to cease from’
περ: περ — even, though; concessive particle, esp. with a participle (= Attic καίπερ) · also used to intensify an adverb or pronoun rather than concede a point: ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’
περίφρων: περίφρων — circumspect, of sound understanding; fem. nom. sg., stock epithet of Penelope
περὶ: περί — around, about; prep. + gen.: ’superior to, beyond’; also as adv.: ’exceedingly, surpassingly’ · also prep. + gen. in its plain sense ’about, concerning’ (περὶ πατρός ’about his father’) · also preverb in tmesis · + dat. · also + acc., of place, ’around, about’ (περὶ ἄστυ ’around the city’)
πηνελόπεια: Πηνελόπεια — Penelope, wife of Odysseus; nom. sg.
ποθέσαι: ποθέω — long for, miss; aor. inf.: ’to miss (him)’
πολλοὶ: πολύς — much, many; masc. nom. pl.
πολλὸν: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially, epic (= Attic πολύ): ’much’
πολύμητις: πολύμητις — of many wiles, epithet of Odysseus (built on μῆτις ’cunning intelligence’); masc. nom. sg.
ποτέ: ποτέ — once, at some time, ever; encl. adv.
πού: πού — somewhere; enclitic adv., weakened to ’I suppose, perhaps’
προσέειπε: προσεῖπον — speak to, address; aor. 3 sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic προσεῖπε)
προσέφη: πρόσφημι — speak to, address; aor. 3 sg.
πρὶν: πρίν — before, until; adv./conj., + inf. (grave, mid-clause form) · also τὸ πρίν, substantivized with the article: ‘formerly, at first’, no infinitive · also bare adv. ’formerly’, no art./inf.
πρὸς: πρός — towards, against, to; prep. + acc.
πόντῳ: πόντος — sea, open sea; dat. sg.
πόσιν: πόσις — husband; acc. sg. · also the distinct noun πόσις ’a drinking, drink’ (from πίνω); acc. sg.: ’drink’ (paired with βρῶσις ’eating’)
πᾶσιν: πᾶς — all, every; masc./neut. dat. pl. (ν-movable)
σ: σύ — you (sg.); encl. acc. sg., elided (σ’ = σε): ’you’
σάμοιό: Σάμος — Same, an island near Ithaca (distinct from Samos in the Aegean); gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
σαώσαι: σαόω (= σῴζω) — save, keep safe; aor. opt. 3 sg., potential without κε/ἄν: ‘could save’
σκιόεντα: σκιόεις — shadowy, dim; neut. acc. pl.
σοὶ: σύ — you (sg.); dat. sg.: ’to, for you’
στῆ: ἵστημι — set, stand; aor. 3 sg., root aorist, unaugmented (= ἔστη): ’stood’
σφ: σφεῖς — they; epic encl. pron., elided σφ’ for dat. σφι ’for them’ or acc. σφε ’them’
σὸς: σός — your, yours (2 sg. possessive); adj., masc. nom. sg.
σὺ: σύ — you (sg.); nom. sg. (grave, mid-clause form)
σὺν: σύν — with, together with; prep. + dat.
σῖτον: σῖτος — bread, grain, the staple of a meal; acc. sg.
τ: τε (elided τ’) — and; ’epic τε’ also marks a standing fact · after οὔ νυ perhaps τοι ’to you’ · also in a question, an expressive epic τε with no connective force, giving a note of doubt or wonder (πῶς τε ...; ’how, pray...?’)
τάδε: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’
τέθνηκε: θνῄσκω — die; perf. 3 sg. with pres. sense: ’is dead’
τέκος: τέκος — child, offspring; neut. voc. sg. (φίλον τέκος ’dear child’)
τέτυκται: τεύχω — make, build; pass. come to pass, happen; perf. pass. 3 sg.: ’has been made, has come to pass’
τήν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. sg., resumptive: ’whom’ · also demonstrative, fem. acc. sg., resuming an earlier noun: ’her’ (τήν … ῥέξω ’her I will sacrifice’)
τίπτε: τίπτε — why ever, what then (= τί ποτε shortened); interrog. adv.
τε: τε — and, both...and; enclitic connective; also ’epic τε’ marking a standing general truth in relative clauses
τεῒν: σύ — you (sg.); epic dat. sg. τεΐν (= Attic σοί)
τηλεμάχῳ: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; masc. dat. sg.
τι: τις, τι — someone, something; neut. acc. sg., used adverbially with negatives ’at all’ · also adjectival indefinite: ’some, any’ (τι δήμιον ἄλλο ’some other public matter’) · also adverbial without a negative: ’in some way, in some measure’ (τι κατὰ πρῆξιν ’on some business’) · also as a substantive object, in a question: ’anything, something’ (ἦ ῥά τι ἴδμεν ’do we know anything’)
τις: τις, τι — someone, something, a certain one; indefinite pron., masc./fem. nom. sg.
τοι: σύ — you (sg.); encl. dat. sg.: ’to/for you’ · also τοι, the affirming particle: ’you know, indeed’ (esp. in ἦ τοι, οὔ τοι); the two are not always easy to keep apart
τοῖον: τοῖος — such, of such a kind; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’in such a way’ · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a noun or pronoun: ’such a one as’ (σέ γε τοῖον ἐγείνατο ’bore a son such as you’) · also ’so’, qualifying an adj.
τοῖσιν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. dat. pl. ’from/to them’
τοῦ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. gen. sg. ’of him, that one’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whose, of whom; masc. gen. sg. (τοῦ νῶι θεοῦ ὣς τερπόμεθ’ αὐδῇ ’whose voice we delight in’)
τόν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg.: ’him’; also relative: ’whom’
τόσσα: τόσος — so much, so many; epic τόσσος (doubled σ), neut. acc. pl.
τὰ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’ · also in the adverbial idiom τὰ πρῶτα, ’at first, first’ (not ’these things’) · also with a noun, pointing to it: ’those, the’ (τὰ σὰ γούνατα ’those knees of yours’)
τὴν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. sg. ’her’
τῆς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun); fem. gen. sg.
τῇ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. dat. sg.: ’her, with her’
τῶν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); gen. pl. ’of these things, of them’
υἷι: υἱός — son; masc. dat. sg., epic υἷι (= Attic υἱεῖ)
φάος: φάος — light (epic uncontracted = Attic φῶς); neut. nom./acc. sg.
φάτο: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented (= ἔφατο)
φίλη: φίλος — dear, one’s own; fem. nom. sg.
φίλον: φίλος — dear, one’s own (with kin/body parts serves as a possessive); neut. nom./acc. sg. · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a masculine noun: φίλον υἱόν ’dear son’
φρένα: φρήν — mind, wits, heart; acc. sg.
φρεσὶ: φρήν — mind, heart, wits; fem. dat. pl.
φρεσὶν: φρήν — mind, heart, wits (lit. midriff); fem. dat. pl.
φόνον: φόνος — murder, slaughter, bloodshed; masc. acc. sg.
φῶτας: φώς — man, warrior, mortal; masc. acc. pl.
χρόα: χρώς — skin, flesh, complexion; acc. sg. χρόα
ἀγορήσατο: ἀγοράομαι — speak in the assembly; aor. 3 sg. mid.
ἀγορεύσω: ἀγορεύω — speak out, declare; fut. 1 sg.
ἀθήνη: Ἀθήνη — Athena, goddess of wisdom and war; nom. sg.
ἀθηναίη: Ἀθηναίη — Athena; fem. nom. sg., epic full form (= Ἀθήνη)
ἀμφιπόλοισι: ἀμφίπολος — handmaid, attendant; fem. dat. pl., epic -οισι
ἀμύμων: ἀμύμων — blameless, excellent (an old epithet whose exact force is uncertain); masc./fem. nom. sg.
ἀνά: ἀνά — up, up along; prep. + acc., or adv. · also as preverb in tmesis (ἀνά … ἔβαινον = ἀνέβαινον ’mounted’); acute kept before an enclitic
ἀνέβαινε: ἀναβαίνω — go up, mount; impf. 3 sg.: ’mounted’
ἀνέρες: ἀνήρ — man; masc. nom. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic ἄνδρες)
ἀναβάντες: ἀναβαίνω — go up, go aboard, embark; aor. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’having embarked’
ἀναβᾶσα: ἀναβαίνω — go up; aor. part. fem. nom. sg.
ἀντίνοος: Ἀντίνοος — Antinous, son of Eupeithes, a leading suitor; masc. nom. sg.
ἀνόρουσε: ἀνορούω — spring up, leap up; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἀνώρουσε)
ἀνὰ: ἀνά — up along, throughout; prep. + acc. · also as preverb in tmesis (ἀνὰ … κέρασσεν, from ἀνακεράννυμι ’mix up’)
ἀπώλεσα: ἀπόλλυμι — destroy, lose; aor. 1 sg. act.: ’I have lost’
ἀρίστους: ἀγαθός — good; superlative ἄριστος, masc. acc. pl.: ’best’
ἀρετῇσι: ἀρετή — excellence, virtue, valor; fem. dat. pl., epic -ῃσι(ν) (= Attic -αις)
ἀφορμηθέντος: ἀφορμάομαι — set out, depart; aor. part. masc. gen. sg., genitive participle governed by ἀκοῦσαι (verb of perception + gen. participle), unexpressed subject ’I’: ’that I have set out’
ἀχαιοί: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, the Greeks; masc. nom. pl.
ἁλὶ: ἅλς — sea, salt water; fem. dat. sg.
ἁλὸς: ἅλς — sea, salt water; fem. gen. sg.
ἂν: ἄν — modal particle marking contingency (with subj. = future contingency, with opt. = potential) · also with a secondary indicative (impf./aor.) marking an unreal, contrary-to-fact conclusion: ’would’ (οὐκ ἂν ... ἀγόρευες ’you would not be speaking’) · also = ἀνά (preposition/preverb ’up’) in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἂν … βαῖνε = ἀνέβαινε, ἂν … βάντες = ἀναβάντες)
ἄγε: ἄγε — come now!; interjectional imper. of ἄγω, 2 sg.
ἄλλ: ἄλλος — other, another; neut. acc. sg., elided (ἄλλ’ = ἄλλο): ’another thing’
ἄλλοι: ἄλλος — other, another; masc. nom. pl.
ἄμμι: ἐγώ (pl. ἡμεῖς) — I, we; epic dat. pl. ἄμμι (= Attic ἡμῖν)
ἄρ: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, elided form ἄρ’ before a vowel
ἄρα: ἄρα — so, as it turned out, then; inferential particle
ἄργος: Ἄργος — Argos, the Argive plain; neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἅμ: ἅμα (elided ἅμ’) — together with, at the same time as; adv./prep. + dat.
ἐείκοσι: εἴκοσι — twenty; numeral, indeclinable, epic prothetic ἐ- (ἐείκοσι = εἴκοσι)
ἐκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as adverb or preverb in tmesis, no case expressed: ’out’ (ἐκ δ’ ἔβαν ’and out they stepped’)
ἐμεῦ: ἐγώ — I; gen. sg., epic (= Attic ἐμοῦ): ’from me’
ἐν: ἐν — in, on, among; + dat.; also used as an adverb, ’in it, there’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐν … βάλῃ = ἐμβάλῃ ’cast in’; ἐν … χεῦον = ἔγχεον ’pour in’)
ἐνόησε: νοέω — perceive, think, devise; aor. 3 sg.
ἐνὶ: ἐν (epic ἐνί) — in, on, among; + dat.
ἐξ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐξ … ἕντο = ἐξέντο, from ἐξίημι ’send out, put away (desire)’)
ἐπ: ἐπί (elided ἐπ’) — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐπ’ … χεῦε = ἐπέχευε ‘poured upon’)
ἐπικεύσω: ἐπικεύθω — hide further, keep back, conceal in addition; fut. 1 sg.
ἐπὶ: ἐπί — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as adverb, no case expressed: ’to it, over it; besides’ (θεοὶ δ’ ἐπὶ μάρτυροι ’witnesses to it’; ἐπὶ κτέρεα κτερεΐξαι ’besides’)
ἐς: εἰς (epic ἐς) — into, to; + acc. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb with no case expressed (ἐς … ἦλθον = εἰσῆλθον ’came in’)
ἐσθλόν: ἐσθλός — good, noble, brave; masc. acc. sg. or neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἐσθλὸν: ἐσθλός — good, noble, brave; neut./masc. acc. sg.
ἐσσι: εἰμί — be; pres. 2 sg., epic (= Attic εἶ)
ἐὺ: ἐΰ — well (Attic εὖ, printed without a diaeresis); adv.
ἑλλάδα: Ἑλλάς — Hellas, here a district of Thessaly; fem. acc. sg.
ἔα: ἐάω — let be, allow, leave alone; pres. imper. 2 sg.: ’leave alone!’
ἔβαν: βαίνω — go, walk; aor. 3 pl., epic (= Attic ἔβησαν)
ἔβη: βαίνω — go, walk, step; aor. 3 sg., root aorist, unaugmented (= ἔβη)
ἔκηε: καίω — burn; aor. 3 sg., Homeric lengthened-vowel form (beside Attic ἔκαυσα): ‘he burned’
ἔκλυεν: κλύω — hear, hear of; aor. 3 sg.
ἔνθ: ἔνθα (elided ἔνθ’) — there, then; adverb of place or time
ἔνθα: ἔνθα — there, then; adverb of place or time · also used relatively, continuing a clause: ’where’ (ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’)
ἔνι: ἐν — in; prep. + dat., postpositive with anastrophe, accent thrown back after its noun (δήμῳ ἔνι = ἐν δήμῳ)
ἔστι: εἰμί — be; pres. 3 sg. impersonal: ’it is possible’ · also existential, ‘there is’ (ἔστι δέ τις πέτρη ‘there is a rock’)
ἠελίοιο: Ἠέλιος — the Sun (god); gen. sg., epic (-οιο = Attic Ἡλίου)
ἠμείβετ: ἀμείβω — exchange; mid. answer, reply; impf. 3 sg. mid. (ἠμείβετο, elided ἠμείβετ’)
ἠρήσαντο: ἀράομαι — pray, wish; aor. mid. 3 pl.
ἠρᾶτο: ἀράομαι — pray, vow; impf. 3 sg., augmented (ἀ- → ἠ-)
ἡ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. nom. sg.: ’she’
ἡδὺ: ἡδύς — sweet, pleasant; adj., neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’sweetly’
ἡμῖν: ἐγώ (pl. ἡμεῖς) — I, we; dat. pl. ’to us’
ἣ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. sg. (grave, mid-clause form)
ἤ: ἤ — or; disjunctive conj., accented before an enclitic (ἤ κεν); ἤ … ἦε ’whether … or’
ἤδη: ἤδη — now, already, at once; adv.
ἤλυθες: ἔρχομαι — come, go; aor. 2 sg., epic ἤλυθες (= Attic ἦλθες): ’you came’
ἥν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; fem. acc. sg. · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whom, which (fem. acc. sg.) · also relative + indefinite, in the compound ἥν τινα = ἥτις (fem.): ’whatever, what’
ἦ: ἦ — truly, verily; affirming particle · also interrogative particle introducing an earnest question · also = ἤ ’or’, in the correlative ἠέ … ἦ ’whether … or’ · also ἠμί — say, speak; unaugmented aor./impf. 3 sg. (= ἔφη), closing or introducing direct speech: ’he/she said’ (ἦ ῥα ’so he said’)
ἧος: ἧος — as long as, while; temporal conj., epic (= Attic ἕως)
ἰάνθη: ἰαίνω — warm, gladden, cheer; aor. pass. 3 sg.: ’was warmed, was gladdened’
ἰκαρίοιο: Ἰκάριος — Icarius, father of Penelope; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
ἱέμενοι: ἵεμαι — long for, strain toward, be eager; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’longing’ (οἴκαδε ἱέμενοι ’longing for home’)
ἱκέσθαι: ἱκνέομαι — come to, reach, arrive at; aor. inf.
ἴσαν: εἶμι — go, come; impf. 3 pl., epic: ’used to go, come’ · also as a simple narrative past, ’went’ (μνηστῆρες … ἴσαν ’the suitors went’), not necessarily iterative
ἵν: ἵνα — so that, in order that; conj., elided (ἵν’ = ἵνα)
ὀίω: ὀΐω — suppose, think (short-form by-word of ὀΐομαι); pres. 1 sg.
ὀδυσσεὺς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus, the poem’s hero; nom. sg.
ὀδυσσῆος: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; gen. sg. (double-σ, metrical variant of single-σ Ὀδυσῆος)
ὀδύρομαι: ὀδύρομαι — lament, mourn, grieve; pres. 1 sg.
ὀιζυρὸν: ὀιζυρός — wretched, full of misery; masc. acc. sg., predicative: ’(bore him) to be wretched’
ὀιζύος: ὀιζύς — woe, misery, hardship; fem. gen. sg., governed by ἔμνησας ’you reminded (me) of’
ὁμάδησαν: ὁμαδέω — make a din, clamor; aor. 3 pl.
ὁππότε: ὁππότε (Attic ὁπότε) — whenever, when; conj., + subj. and κε in a general temporal clause · also introducing an indirect question, + pres. indic.: ’when’ (ὁππότε Τηλέμαχος νεῖτ(αι) ’when Telemachus is to return’)
ὁρμαίνοντες: ὁρμαίνω — ponder, turn over in the mind, debate; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’pondering’
ὃ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ (relative) — who, which; neut. nom./acc. sg., referring to a person: ’that he...’ · also masc. nom. sg. relative, ’who’, used in address with a 2nd person verb (ὃ χθιζὸς θεὸς ἤλυθες ’you who came yesterday as a god’)
ὄσσε: ὄσσε — the two eyes; neut. dual noun, no sg., epic (= Attic ὄμματα)
ὅ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. sg.; with γε: ’he’ · also relative, masc. nom. sg., accented before an enclitic: ’who’ (ὅ κε ... ἐφείη) · also = ὅτι ’that’; εἰς ὅ ’until’ · also relative, neut. nom./acc. sg.: ’which’ (ὅ οἱ πέρι δῶκεν Ἀθήνη ’which Athena gave her beyond others’)
ὅς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.)
ὅσσ: ὅσος (epic ὅσσος, double σ) — as much/many as; neut. acc. pl., elided (ὅσσ’ = ὅσσα): ’as much as’ · also neut. nom. pl., subject of a verb: ὅσσ’ ἐπὶ γαῖαν ἑρπετὰ γίγνονται ’as many creatures as come to be upon earth’
ὅσσα: ὅσος — as much/many as; epic ὅσσος (double σ), neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’as many as’
ὑγρὰ: ὑγρός — wet, fluid, liquid; neut. acc. pl.
ὑπερηνορεόντων: ὑπερηνορέω — play the overbearing man, be overweening (ὑπέρ + ἀνήρ); pres. part. gen. pl., epic uncontracted, partitive with τις
ὑπερφιάλοισι: ὑπερφίαλος — overbearing, arrogant; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
ὑπερφιάλους: ὑπερφίαλος — overbearing, arrogant, presumptuous; masc. acc. pl.
ὑπερῷ: ὑπερῷον — upper story, upper chamber; neut. acc. pl., elided (ὑπερῷ’ = ὑπερῷα)
ὑπὲρ: ὑπέρ — over, beyond; + acc. (ὑπὲρ μόρον ’beyond one’s portion’) · also + gen., literally ’over, above’ (ὑπὲρ ἀργυρέοιο λέβητος ’over a silver basin’)
ὑπὸ: ὑπό — under, beneath; prep. + dat./acc.; also used as an adverb, ’beneath’ · also as preverb in tmesis (ὑπὸ … ἐδήσατο = ὑπεδήσατο ’bound beneath’) · also adverbial, of breeding: ’begotten under, born of’ (ὑπὸ δ’ ἡμίονοι ’and under them [the mares], mules’)
ὡς: ὡς — as, how, that, when; with the optative introduces a wish: ’so may…’ (unaccented; accented ὥς / ὣς is ’thus’) · also ὡς + unaugmented ὄφελον + inf., an unfulfillable wish: ’would that...’ · also ὡς + opt., a purpose clause (= ἵνα): ’so that’ (ὡς τὸν χόλον ἐξακέσαιτο ’so that he might appease the anger’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. + inf.: ’how (good, etc.) it is to...’ (ὡς ἀγαθὸν ... λιπέσθαι ’how good a thing it is to be left behind’) · also plain ὡς + indic., ’as’ (ὡς σὺ κελεύεις ’as you command’) or ’how’ in an indirect question (ὡς ἐπὶ πόντον ἐλεύσομαι ’how I shall come upon the sea’)
ὣς: ὥς — thus, so; adverb (accented, distinct from unaccented ὡς ’as’; = Attic οὕτως) · also postpositive after its noun (anastrophe), = comparative ὡς ’as, like’: ὄρνις δ’ ὥς ’like a bird’
ὥρμισαν: ὁρμίζω — moor, bring to anchor; aor. 3 pl.: ’they moored (her)’
ὥς: ὥς — thus, so; also (with κε/ἄν + subj.) ’so that, in order that’; adverb/conjunction · also introducing an indirect question: ’how’ (ὥς κε νέηται ’how he is to return’, after φράσσεται) · or ὡς ’as’, accented before enclitic τε
ὧδε: ὧδε — here, to this place, in this way; adv.
ῥ: ἄρα (weakened ῥα, elided ῥ’) — then, indeed, so; inferential particle
